artworks.title: Captain Thomas Weaver of Armagh
artworks.description: The image is a portrait showing the upper body of a man facing forward. He has refined facial features, including a prominent nose and direct gaze. He has long wavy hair past his shoulders and wears clothing typical of the 17th century. There are no accessories or objects in his hands. The background is an oval frame with intricate engraved lines and leafy patterns.

artworks.title: Henry Welby
artworks.description: The image depicts an elderly man seated on a chair with flowing hair and a long beard. He is leaning forward, resting his head on his left hand on the armrest. The man wears a loose garment and has one foot on a footrest. He holds a cane in his right hand. On the table in front of him, there is an open book and a fabric-covered box. Above him, there is a wooden shelf with stacked books. In the background, there is a window showing outdoor activities. The floor has a checkered design.

artworks.title: Thomas Wolsey, Cardinal, Archibishop of York
artworks.description: The image shows a man in profile facing left. His upper body is turned slightly toward the viewer. He has a prominent nose, a defined chin, and closed lips, with eyes looking ahead. He wears a beret-like hat covering most of his short hair. He is dressed in a robe with a high collar and buttons down the shoulder. He holds a rolled-up piece of paper or parchment in his left hand. The background has a textured pattern. An inscription at the bottom of the image identifies him as Thomas Wolsey, with framing lines giving a formal presentation.

artworks.title: Title page to R. Brathwait, A Survey of History
artworks.description: This is an engraving of a historical-themed frontispiece. The central focus is a portrait of a man, surrounded by elaborate illustrations and inscriptions. The upper section bears the title, "A Survey of History or A Nursery for Gentry." Flanking this title are depictions of historians such as Herodotus, Thucydides, T. Livius, and C. Tacitus, each represented in small archways with symbols or scenes suggestive of their historical contributions. Below the central portrait, there is printed information indicating this work was produced by N. and John Okes in London in 1638. This engraving is likely used as an introductory page for a historical book or collection.

artworks.title: Title page to Richard Brathwait, English Gentleman and English Gentlewoman
artworks.description: The image features two full-length figures, a man and a woman, standing in niches with columns on either side. The man stands confidently with one hand on his hip, wearing a large brimmed hat, a cape, knee-length boots, and holding a cane. His facial features include a mustache, goatee, and shoulder-length wavy hair. The adjacent text block is titled "The English Gentleman and English Gentlevvoman" by Richard Brathwait, Esquire, printed in London by John Dawson in 1631. The woman is depicted with long wavy hair, wearing a gown and holding a small object. Surrounding the central figures are smaller compartments illustrating themes like "Youth," "Disposition," "Apparel," "Behaviour," "Education," "Vocation," filled with corresponding imagery like a ship, musical instruments, and allegorical figures. The background is dense with illustrative and textual elements, conveying a sense of historical and cultural richness.

artworks.title: Title page to Thomas Fuller, Holy State
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a title page for the book "The Holy State" by Thomas Fuller. The design includes figures representing Truth and Justice, an architectural motif with arches and columns labeled "The Church" and "The State," and a map of England at the center. The upper part of the drawing has allegorical figures under the words "TRUTH" and "JUSTICE." The central portrait is above the title, and the bottom text provides publication details, stating it was printed in Cambridge in 1648 by R.D. for John Williams, at the sign of the Crowne in St. Paule's Church-yard, with the artist W. Marshall named as the engraver.

artworks.title: Title page to J.L. Guez, Sieur du Balzack, New Epistles
artworks.description: The image features a bust of a man on a pedestal. The man has medium-length, curly hair and a mustache, with defined facial features including a prominent nose and expressive eyes. He is wearing a dark garment with a wide, white, pointed collar. To the left of the bust is a figure of a man in a classical warrior's attire, complete with a helmet adorned with wings and carrying a caduceus. To the right of the bust is a female figure dressed in draped clothing, holding a quill pen and a book or scroll. The background includes an inscribed panel with text related to new epistles and their translation, mentioning London and a publication date of 1638. The setting appears to be a formal or classical scene with detailed engravings and ornamental elements.

artworks.title: Sir Thomas More, Epigrammata
artworks.description: The image shows an engraved portrait of a man in an ornate oval frame. The man has prominent features and is wearing a hat and fur-collared robe. Flanking the frame are a female figure and a male figure. Below the portrait is a Latin inscription, with publisher and engraver names at the bottom. The engraving is in black and white.

artworks.title: Title Page to Francis Quarles, Shepherds Oracles
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a tree surrounded by various symbolic figures. The image depicts a tree labeled 'Religion', with branches labeled 'Faith', 'Obedience', 'Hope', and 'Charitie', and fruit labeled 'Good works'. Several figures interact with the tree: Two individuals sit on the branches holding axes, one individual holds a book labeled 'Schoole Candies', and below are figures, some holding tools. On the left, a crowned figure points a sword at the trunk.

artworks.title: Bust of Earl of Monmouth
artworks.description: The image shows a bust of a man. The bust is in profile facing left, displaying only one side of his facial features. The man has a prominent nose, mustache, and wavy hair that falls just below his ears. He appears to be wearing a garment with ruffled or patterned edges. The base of the bust sits on a pedestal with inscriptions stating "Henricus Dom: CARY; Baro de Lepington; Com: de Monmouth." The background features hills, trees, and a building resembling a church with a pointed roof surrounded by trees. The style of the image is detailed engraving.

artworks.title: Title Page to J.F. Lenault, The Use of the Passions
artworks.description: This is a drawing of figures representing various emotions connected to Reason and Divine Grace. The figures are labeled with names such as "Fear," "Joy," "Sorrow," and "Choler." They are linked by chains to a central female figure representing Reason, who is advised by Divine Grace from above. Each emotion is engaged in a symbolic activity reflecting its nature. The detailed scene conveys the relationship between human passions, reason, and divine grace. The style and labeling suggest a didactic or illustrative purpose, possibly conveying moral or philosophical ideas visually.

artworks.title: Title Page to Sir Thomas Smith, The Commonwealth of England
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a title page for a book. The title page displays the text "THE COMMONWEALTH OF ENGLAND BY The Honourable Sir Tho: Smith, Knight. Newly Corrected & Amended." The text is surrounded by decorative elements, including two cherubic figures with wings and trumpets at the top holding up an oval portrait of a crowned figure. Pillars frame the central text, and two allegorical female figures flank the pillars; one holds a sword, and the other holds a ship. Beneath the text is a detailed map with symbols and geographic shapes, labeled "Will. Marshall, Sculptist."

artworks.title: Title Page from Xenophon’s Cyrupaedia
artworks.description: The image shows two full-length figures and an additional portrait in an engraving. On the left, an armored warrior stands gesturing and holding a long spear. On the right, a crowned figure with curly hair, wearing an ornate robe with a high collar, holds a scepter. Both figures flank a text block with a portrait of a bearded man labeled "Xenophon." Below this, a framed portrait depicts an older man in Elizabethan attire seated and holding a paper. The background includes architectural columns and arches, as well as labeled plinths beneath each figure.

artworks.title: Thomas Howard, Earl of Arundel
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman after Sir Anthony van Dyck
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing from the chest up. He has curly dark hair falling to ear level, a beard, and a mustache. His facial features include deep-set eyes and a serious expression. The man wears formal attire with a white collar under a dark cloak. A circular medallion hangs around his neck. The background is a dark, textured surface.

artworks.title: Charles I
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the waist up. He is positioned with his body slightly turned to the side, but his head is facing forward. He has a composed facial expression with detailed eyes, nose, and a mustache. His hair is curly, shoulder-length, and neatly arranged around his face. He is wearing a richly adorned outfit featuring an extravagant lace ruff around his neck and an intricately patterned doublet with vertical striped elements, buttons, and a pendant. The artwork style gives texture and depth to both the clothing and facial features. The background is a simple, subtle, and dark shade, highlighting the figure in the foreground.

artworks.title: Desiderius Erasmus
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman after Hans Holbein the Younger
artworks.description: The image shows a man in a bust view, seated and facing slightly to his left with a serene expression. He has defined facial features, short wavy hair, and wears a fur-trimmed cloak. The background has a detailed textured pattern.

artworks.title: Desiderius Erasmus
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman after Hans Holbein the Younger
artworks.description: The image shows an upper body portrait of a man seated with his hands crossed in front of him. His face is shown in profile to the left, with prominent cheekbones, a pointed nose, and a slightly furrowed brow. He has visible wrinkles around his eyes and mouth. His hair appears to be short and curly underneath a round, flat cap. He is wearing a long, dark robe with a thick, fur collar, and a light fabric wrapped around his neck. There is no jewelry visible. The background is a plain, textured surface, and the bottom of the image has text that reads "DESIDERIUS ERASMUS ROTTERODAMUS".

artworks.title: Desiderius Erasmus
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman after Hans Holbein the Younger
artworks.description: The image shows an upper half portrait of Desiderius Erasmus Rotterodamus. He is seated with his body slightly turned towards the left. His facial features are distinct, with a long straight nose, prominent cheekbones, and a slight smile. He has wavy hair that peeks out from underneath a large, soft hat that fits snugly on his head. He is wearing a coat with a luxurious fur trim, and his hands are folded gently in front of him, partially covered by the coat's long sleeves. The background of the image is a simple, textured surface. The name "Desiderius Erasmus Rotterodamus" is prominently displayed at the bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Richard Kingston, Political Pamphleteer, Chaplain to Charles I
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman or Lucas Vorsterman II
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man. He is portrayed from the chest up, facing slightly left and looking directly at the viewer. The man has long, wavy hair, a high forehead, large eyes, and a firm mouth. He is wearing a dark garment with a white collar. Surrounding the person's image is an ornamental border with text, and in the background, there are books and possibly a curtain, indicating an interior space with elements suggestive of study. A coat of arms with intricate designs is visible on the left side.

artworks.title: William, First Duke of Newcastle
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of a man with only his shoulders and head visible. He is facing slightly to the right while his body is turned slightly to the left. The man has a long face with strong cheekbones, a narrow mustache, and wavy hair that falls to his shoulders. He is wearing a high-collared shirt with a large decorative ruffle and a doublet or coat detailed on the shoulders and chest. Two decorative loops hang from his clothing at the shoulders, and he wears a medallion around his neck. The background consists of an oval frame with Latin text surrounding the portrait, engraved in a textured pattern.

artworks.title: Thomas Howard, Third Duke of Norfolk
artworks.artist: Lucas Emil Vorsterman after Hans Holbein the Elder
artworks.description: The image depicts a man in an upper body portrait, facing slightly to the viewer's right, holding a staff in each hand. He has a long face with a solemn expression, short, wavy hair, and a large hat. He wears a richly decorated garment with a broad, ornate fur collar and a garment clasp across his chest. He has a chain with a decorative medallion around his neck. The background has a textured, cross-hatched pattern.

artworks.title: Abraham Aurelius, Minister of the French Church in London
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing from just below the waist up. He is in a poised position, with his left hand resting on a table holding an open book and his right hand holding a closed book. The man has a full beard and mustache, closely cropped hair, and a solemn expression. He is wearing a period-appropriate robe with large sleeves, detailed buttons, and a ruffled collar. There is no visible jewelry. The background has a vertical textured pattern on the right side. The portrait is framed by text above and below.

artworks.title: Christian, Duke of Brunswick
artworks.artist: Robert van Voerst after Sir Anthony van Dyck
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of a man from the waist up, posed in a three-quarter view to the right. He has loose, wavy hair that falls to his collar, framing a face with a serious expression, featuring a mustache and fine features. He is dressed in a detailed outfit, wearing armor adorned with studs or rivets and a sash draped over one shoulder, with a large collar that appears to be made of lace. He has a long sword visible by his side that is decorated with an emblem near the hilt. In the background, there are depictions of foliage and clouds, adding a touch of nature and depth to the portrait's setting.

artworks.title: William Fielding, First Earl of Denbigh
artworks.artist: Robert van Voerst after Sir Anthony van Dyck
artworks.description: The image shows a man in a bust-length portrait within an oval frame. He is facing slightly to the right with a serious expression. He has a beard, mustache, long curly hair, and wears an elaborate outfit with a lace collar, doublet, and sash. The portrait is highly detailed with intricate line work, and the background inside the oval frame has a dot and line pattern. There is a decorative border with text in capital letters surrounding the oval. Below the image, there is a wider border with a script revealing the man's name, titles, engraver's attribution, and the year "1631".
